title: Hadith Knowledge
description: Little Muslim → Pro. Short questions develop simple hadith-reading skills and connect familiar teachings with thoughtful conduct. Covers narrator and compiler roles, reading collection references, seeking informed explanation, beneficial companionship, mutual support, shared compassion, small kindnesses, gratitude, helping others and Allah’s help, choosing a clear alternative, guiding others to good, valuing health and free time, haya, arrogance, belongings, careful speech, food’s blessing, dua for others, confidentiality and modest gifts. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar terms. All questions are Pro level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Pro is the highest editorial level within Little Muslim, not the Educated User level. It emphasizes connecting a teaching with its purpose, understanding a simple comparison, distinguishing related ideas and applying a lesson to a brief situation. All three question styles remain Kids Pro level; styles are not difficulty tiers. Supplied reference labels are reading examples, not a requirement to memorize hadith numbers or narrator biographies. No technical chain analysis, independent authentication, specialist legal disputes or obscure historical dates are required. The bank has not been calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked reports from Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Jami at-Tirmidhi and Sunan Abi Dawud, and Sunnah.com's own collection and explanatory pages were checked during preparation. Tirmidhi 1954 and 2518 are labeled Sahih (Darussalam), Tirmidhi 1959 Hasan (Darussalam) and Abi Dawud 5003 Hasan (Al-Albani) on the linked pages; these are attributed source gradings, not independent authentication. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Present-day situations are illustrative applications rather than narrated events or complete legal rulings. The narrator example distinguishes Umar, the companion reporting that he heard the Prophet, from the later collection compiler, without claiming the report has only one transmitter. Reference reading follows the linked site's displayed collection numbering and does not assume fixed pagination or identical numbering across editions. Seeking a knowledgeable teacher does not authorize rejecting a report merely because it seems unfamiliar. The perfume comparison concerns a companion's influence, not a judgment of a worker's occupation, income, physical smell or human worth. The building and body comparisons encourage mutual support and concern, without requiring children to bear adult burdens, learn private details or enter unsafe situations. The cheerful-face example does not require constant smiling or judge disability, distress, personality or inner faith by facial appearance. Thanking people accompanies gratitude to Allah rather than replacing it or excusing harmful demands. The link between helping others and Allah’s help encourages suitable support, without requiring children to carry dangerous loads, manage adult problems or neglect their own needs. The doubtful-matter questions concern a genuine uncertainty with a clear alternative, not intrusive thoughts, ordinary anxiety, imagined prohibitions or endless checking after clarification. The reward for guiding to good is not presented as taking reward away from another person or a reason to withhold practical help. The health-and-free-time teaching encourages gratitude and thoughtful use of opportunities, without condemning ordinary play, suitable rest, illness or disability; health is not treated as proof of superior faith. Haya is taught as modest restraint from wrongdoing, not a reason to hide harm, avoid necessary questions or label a shy child as better than another. The arrogance report distinguishes contempt and rejection of truth from simply enjoying presentable clothes; no individual's hidden heart or final salvation is judged. The belongings report concerns wrongful taking, including pranks, without classifying every mistake or permitted borrowing as theft. The speech warning encourages care without declaring a particular child's spiritual fate or treating every accidental word as a catastrophe. The food questions draw on the report's reminder of blessing; sensible portions are an educational application, not a quotation or an instruction to eat unsafe food, exceed one's needs or ignore illness. Dua for an absent Muslim is taught through the angel's response without unsupported guarantees, publicity requirements or treating kindness toward others as forbidden. Confidentiality concerns entrusted ordinary information; danger, abuse or risk of harm should be brought to a trusted adult, and secrecy is not made absolute. The modest-gift questions concern appreciation without requiring unsafe acceptance, a costly return gift or assigning monetary thresholds to kindness. This remains a draft for scholarly and child-readability review, not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: A page names Umar as narrator and al-Bukhari as compiler. Who heard and reported the Prophet's ﷺ words in this report?

options.text: Umar
Al-Bukhari
The page translator
The app designer

questions.explanation: Umar reported hearing the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Bukhari later compiled the report in his collection; these are different roles.

questions.question: In the reference Sahih al-Bukhari 8, what does the number help you find?

options.text: The narrator's age
The report in the named collection
The number of daily prayers
The page in every printed edition

questions.explanation: The collection name and reference number help locate a report. A hadith reference is not a fixed page number for every edition.

questions.question: When a hadith seems difficult to understand or apply, whose informed explanation should you seek?

options.text: Whoever has the most followers
Whoever answers fastest without checking
A knowledgeable, trustworthy teacher or scholar's
Only your own first guess

questions.explanation: Hadith need careful understanding. A knowledgeable teacher or scholar can explain the context and how the teaching should be applied.

questions.question: In the hadith comparing companions, what represents a good companion's beneficial influence?

options.text: A person carrying empty boxes
A person counting market stalls
A person measuring a road
A person carrying musk perfume

questions.explanation: The pleasant perfume illustrates beneficial company. The comparison helps us think about how companions can influence our conduct.

questions.question: What image does the hadith use for believers strengthening one another?

options.text: Parts of a building supporting each other
Separate islands with no connection
Clouds moving in opposite directions
Coins competing to shine brightest

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ compared believers' support to a building whose parts strengthen each other. Mutual help makes the community stronger.

questions.question: What does the hadith compare believers' mutual love and compassion to?

options.text: A collection of unrelated stones
One body responding when a part hurts
A race with only one winner
A tree with no branches

questions.explanation: The comparison describes shared concern. Just as a body responds to pain in one part, believers should care about one another's suffering.

questions.question: Which small act of goodness does the hadith specifically say we should not dismiss?

options.text: Waiting to be greeted by someone important
Saving kindness only for special occasions
Meeting a fellow Muslim with a cheerful face
Measuring friendship by expensive presents

questions.explanation: A warm expression can be a meaningful kindness. Goodness is not limited to costly or dramatic actions.

questions.question: The hadith links gratitude to Allah with which response toward people who help us?

options.text: Keeping their help secret from them
Expecting even more from them
Comparing their help with someone else's
Thanking them

questions.explanation: The hadith connects gratitude to Allah with gratitude toward people. Recognizing someone's kindness is part of a thankful attitude.

questions.question: According to the hadith, Allah helps His servant while that person is doing what?

options.text: Helping a fellow Muslim
Competing for everyone's attention
Waiting to be praised before helping
Ignoring every difficulty outside their home

questions.explanation: The report links helping a fellow Muslim with Allah's help. Caring action is valuable even when it does not bring public attention.

questions.question: When an action is genuinely doubtful, what choice does the hadith encourage?

options.text: Choose it simply because friends insist
Leave it for a clear, sound alternative
Treat uncertainty as proof that it is best
Make every ordinary action feel doubtful

questions.explanation: The teaching encourages leaving a doubtful matter for what is clear. It is not an invitation to invent doubts about everything.

questions.question: What reward does the hadith describe for someone who guides another person to a good deed?

options.text: Only the praise of the people watching
A share taken away from the other person's reward
A reward like that of the person doing it
No reward unless they perform every step themselves

questions.explanation: Guiding someone toward good is itself valuable. The hadith describes a reward like that of the person who does the good deed.

questions.question: Which two blessings does the hadith warn that many people fail to use well?

options.text: Popularity and expensive clothes
Travel and large houses
Strength and winning every contest
Health and free time

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ named health and free time as blessings often undervalued. Recognizing their value can guide thoughtful choices.

questions.question: What does the hadith say haya, or good modesty, brings?

options.text: Goodness
Permission to mistreat quiet people
A reason to hide every question
A need to avoid all learning

questions.explanation: Haya is a sense of modesty that helps us avoid wrongdoing. The hadith praises it as a source of good.

questions.question: A man asked about enjoying nice clothes and shoes. Did the Prophet ﷺ define that alone as arrogance?

options.text: Yes; every neat outfit proves someone is arrogant
No; he distinguished beauty from contempt and rejecting truth
Yes; comfortable shoes are always a sign of pride
No; arrogance means only speaking in a loud voice

questions.explanation: The warning concerns refusing truth and treating people with contempt. Enjoying neat clothes is not by itself the arrogance described here.

questions.question: What does the hadith forbid even when someone claims to be joking?

options.text: Sharing an approved game with friends
Offering to lend your own pencil
Taking another person's belongings without right
Asking before borrowing a book

questions.explanation: The report warns against taking another person's property as a joke or seriously. Something taken should be returned.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach about words a person says without considering their importance?

options.text: They never matter if said quickly
They matter only when written down
They are harmless whenever others laugh
They can have serious spiritual consequences

questions.explanation: The report describes both rewarding and harmful speech. Words deserve care even when the speaker treats them as unimportant.

questions.question: Why does the hadith encourage care even with small portions of food?

options.text: We do not know where its blessing lies
Only the largest portions can contain blessing
Every meal must include expensive ingredients
A person must always eat more than needed

questions.explanation: The report reminds us that we do not know where the blessing in food lies. Food deserves care rather than thoughtless disregard.

questions.question: When a Muslim sincerely prays for another Muslim in their absence, what does the angel say for the person praying?

options.text: That only public duas are accepted
That they may receive the same good
That their friend now owes them a gift
That kindness must be kept for relatives

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages dua for another Muslim who is absent. The angel asks that the same good be granted to the one praying.

questions.question: In the hadith about private speech, what can looking around while speaking indicate?

options.text: The listener may announce it to everyone
The speaker wants a public competition
The conversation is being entrusted to the listener
The information must be turned into a joke

questions.explanation: The report teaches care with speech given in confidence. A sign of privacy should not be treated as permission to spread it.

questions.question: What attitude does the hadith discourage toward a neighbor's modest gift?

options.text: Appreciating the neighbor's thoughtfulness
Thanking the giver sincerely
Treating the giver respectfully
Looking down on it because it is small

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against belittling a neighbor's gift, even a very small one. Its price is not the whole measure of kindness.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Umar's role from al-Bukhari's in the intentions report?

options.text: Umar narrated it; al-Bukhari compiled it
Al-Bukhari heard it directly from the Prophet ﷺ
Umar translated al-Bukhari's book into English
The narrator and compiler must always be the same person

questions.explanation: The report identifies Umar as the companion who heard the Prophet ﷺ. The collection was compiled later by al-Bukhari.

questions.question: Which information makes Sahih al-Bukhari 8 more useful to look up than the number 8 alone?

options.text: The number proves every translation uses identical words
The number is paired with its collection name
The number tells us the report's length
The number identifies the reader's score

questions.explanation: A number needs its collection and numbering system to be useful. A reference helps us find and check the relevant report.

questions.question: Why can reading one translated hadith be insufficient for deciding a detailed religious ruling?

options.text: A short translation always contains every relevant detail
The reader's favorite answer settles the issue
Context and related teachings may need scholarly explanation
Popularity removes the need to understand the report

questions.explanation: Careful interpretation considers more than an isolated line. Scholars explain how reports and other relevant evidence fit together.

questions.question: What is the main point of the perfume comparison about companions?

options.text: A person's job alone proves their character
Only friends who give presents are valuable
A pleasant smell guarantees a truthful person
Company can influence us for good or harm

questions.explanation: The comparison is about influence, not judging people by occupation or smell. Good company can encourage good conduct.

questions.question: Which idea best fits the hadith's image of a strong building?

options.text: People strengthen one another through mutual support
The strongest person never needs anyone's help
One member's success requires everyone else to fail
Helping matters only when it attracts attention

questions.explanation: The building's parts work together. The image encourages cooperation and support rather than isolated competition.

questions.question: Which response best matches the hadith's comparison of believers to one body?

options.text: A problem matters only when it affects our home
Another person's suffering should concern us too
Caring means pretending everyone's pain is identical
Compassion requires knowing every private detail

questions.explanation: The image emphasizes shared compassion. We can care about someone's difficulty without assuming we know exactly how they feel.

questions.question: What broader lesson follows from the hadith's example of a cheerful face?

options.text: A person must look cheerful every moment
Only visible smiles count as kindness
Small acts of kindness should not be underestimated
Quiet people cannot show goodwill

questions.explanation: A warm greeting illustrates small goodness. The lesson does not require a constant smile or judging someone's feelings from their face.

questions.question: Which statement fits the hadith about thanking people?

options.text: Thanking a helper replaces gratitude to Allah
Only paid helpers deserve acknowledgment
A small favor never deserves thanks
Thanking people belongs alongside gratitude to Allah

questions.explanation: Gratitude to Allah and appreciation for people's kindness belong together. A helper's effort can deserve acknowledgment even when the favor is small.

questions.question: What does the hadith linking our help for others with Allah's help encourage?

options.text: Responding to another person's needs with suitable support
Helping only when a favor will be returned
Avoiding every task that benefits someone else
Taking over every adult problem by ourselves

questions.explanation: The teaching encourages active support. A child can help within their ability and seek an adult when someone needs more assistance.

questions.question: Which approach best fits leaving a doubtful matter for a clear alternative?

options.text: Keep inventing doubts after a matter has been clarified
Choose what is clearly appropriate and seek guidance if needed
Follow pressure instead of asking a useful question
Assume every nervous feeling proves something is wrong

questions.explanation: The teaching supports clear, sound choices. Ordinary nervousness and repeated worries are not themselves proof that an action is wrong.

questions.question: What does the reward for guiding someone to good show?

options.text: Only the person receiving public credit can be rewarded
Advice is valuable even when it directs people to harm
Helping good happen can matter beyond doing it yourself
Helping someone requires doing every task in their place

questions.explanation: We can contribute by showing a useful path to good. Guiding and doing are different ways of helping goodness happen.

questions.question: Which understanding fits the hadith about health and free time?

options.text: Rest and suitable play are always wasted time
Illness proves someone failed to be grateful
Every spare minute must become a competition
Value available opportunities and use them thoughtfully

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages valuing these blessings. Thoughtful use of time can include suitable rest, play, learning and worship without judging people who are ill.

questions.question: Which distinction helps explain the haya praised in the hadith?

options.text: Avoiding wrongdoing differs from being afraid to seek help
Good modesty requires hiding every mistake from a teacher
Feeling nervous always means a person is more righteous
Learning becomes wrong when a question feels embarrassing

questions.explanation: The praised modesty supports good conduct. It should not become a reason to refuse necessary help or avoid honest learning.

questions.question: Which contrast matches the hadith's explanation of arrogance?

options.text: Simple clothes always prove a humble heart
Neat clothes can be fine; rejecting truth is a problem
Expensive shoes make every action wrong
Winning an argument proves someone's moral worth

questions.explanation: The hadith distinguishes enjoying a good appearance from refusing truth and despising people. We should assess conduct without judging hidden hearts.

questions.question: Why does calling the taking of someone's property a joke fail to excuse it?

options.text: A joke automatically creates permission
Only expensive belongings have an owner
The owner's rights still matter
Returning it later makes every method acceptable

questions.explanation: The report includes both joking and serious taking. Another person's rights do not disappear because the taker intended amusement.

questions.question: Which distinction follows from the hadith about careless words?

options.text: A short remark can never have lasting effects
A large audience makes harmful speech acceptable
Careless speech matters only when the speaker is famous
A remark's impact can exceed the speaker's attention to it

questions.explanation: The speaker may give a remark little thought while its consequences are serious. Careful speech involves more than judging a sentence's length.

questions.question: Which conclusion fits the hadith's reminder about blessing in food?

options.text: A small amount of food can deserve thoughtful care
Only costly food can be blessed
Every leftover must be eaten despite illness or danger
A larger plate always brings greater blessing

questions.explanation: The report encourages respect for food. It does not tell children to ignore safety, illness or their body's limits.

questions.question: What does the hadith about dua in someone's absence encourage?

options.text: Praying for others only when they are listening
Wishing good for others without needing their applause
Making a public record of every private dua
Expecting a reward from the person prayed for

questions.explanation: Dua can express sincere goodwill when the other person is absent. Kindness does not need to be performed for their praise.

questions.question: Which lesson fits the hadith's description of a confidential conversation?

options.text: Everything said quietly must be shared as news
Private details become public once one person hears them
Treat entrusted information with care
Keeping confidence requires hiding danger from trusted adults

questions.explanation: The report teaches trust with private speech. It does not require children to conceal harm or avoid help from trusted adults.

questions.question: Which distinction fits the hadith about a neighbor's small gift?

options.text: Only gifts of equal price can show friendship
Receiving something small means the giver dislikes you
A grateful response must include an expensive return gift
A gift's modest price does not erase its kindness

questions.explanation: A modest gift can still carry thoughtfulness. The hadith discourages contempt rather than turning kindness into a price comparison.

questions.question: Your quiz card swaps Umar and al-Bukhari's roles in the intentions report. Which correction should you make?

options.text: Label Umar narrator and al-Bukhari collection compiler
Label al-Bukhari the companion who heard the Prophet ﷺ
Label Umar the English translator of the collection
Remove all names because roles do not matter

questions.explanation: Correct labels distinguish the companion reporting the Prophet's ﷺ words from the later compiler. They help a learner read references carefully.

questions.question: A teacher gives you Sahih al-Bukhari 8 to check. What is the best first step?

options.text: Open page eight of any book
Open the named collection and find that reference
Search only for eight without a collection name
Assume every collection's eighth report has the same content

questions.explanation: Use the collection name with the reference number. If an edition uses different numbering, ask for help matching the report.

questions.question: Two short hadith translations seem to point in different directions. What should you do before deciding what they mean?

options.text: Choose the version that asks the least of you
Declare one false solely because you feel confused
Ask a knowledgeable teacher to explain their context together
Invent a rule that neither report states

questions.explanation: Bring the actual references to a knowledgeable teacher. Confusion is a reason to seek explanation rather than rush to a ruling.

questions.question: One friend encourages honesty; another pressures you to cheat. What applies the hadith about companions?

options.text: Copy the cheating to preserve every friendship
Judge both friends only by their clothes
Assume all their actions must be the same
Seek supportive company and refuse pressure to cheat

questions.explanation: The comparison teaches that company influences us. Seek encouragement toward good, and ask a trusted adult for help with harmful pressure.

questions.question: Your class has an approved group task. What reflects the hadith's building comparison?

options.text: Share tasks fairly and help teammates make progress
Hide useful information to look strongest
Leave every difficult part to one person
Treat a teammate's difficulty as entertainment

questions.explanation: Parts of a building strengthen one another. Fair cooperation in a suitable task is a simple way to apply mutual support.

questions.question: A classmate misses lessons because of a family difficulty. What applies the hadith about shared compassion?

options.text: Demand every private detail before showing care
Ask an adult about a thoughtful way to support them
Ignore them because your own family is fine
Tell them their difficulty must feel exactly like yours

questions.explanation: Shared compassion means noticing another person's hardship. With adult guidance, you can offer help while respecting their privacy and feelings.

questions.question: You have no gift for a friend arriving at an activity. What fits the hadith about small goodness?

options.text: Avoid them because kindness requires money
Wait until someone important greets them first
Offer a warm greeting and make them feel welcome
Explain that greetings have no value without presents

questions.explanation: A cheerful meeting is a valued example of goodness. A kind welcome can matter even when you have nothing to give.

questions.question: A classmate explains a difficult homework instruction. What applies the hadith about gratitude?

options.text: Thank only when the whole class is watching
Assume helping you was their permanent duty
Complain that they should have helped earlier
Thank Allah and also thank your classmate

questions.explanation: Appreciating a person's help fits gratitude to Allah. A sincere thank-you recognizes the effort they made.

questions.question: A classmate needs help carrying a few light books. What applies the hadith about helping others and Allah's help?

options.text: Offer suitable help within your ability
Demand public praise before touching a book
Assume small help can never matter
Take a dangerous load to prove your sincerity

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages helping others. Suitable help can be simple; children should respect their limits and ask an adult for larger needs.

questions.question: You are unsure whether a pen is yours, but your own labeled pen is available. What fits choosing a clear alternative?

options.text: Take the uncertain pen because it looks newer
Use your labeled pen and ask about the other one
Hide both pens until nobody asks
Assume not knowing the owner makes it yours

questions.explanation: Using the pen known to be yours is a clear alternative. A simple question can clarify ownership without endless worry.

questions.question: A friend wants to join an approved charity activity but cannot find the teacher. What applies guiding someone to good?

options.text: Hide the location to keep the reward for yourself
Tell them help counts only if it is expensive
Show them where the supervising teacher is
Make up a different meeting place as a joke

questions.explanation: Pointing someone toward a suitable good activity can itself be valuable. You do not have to do every part on their behalf.

questions.question: You have a free afternoon and feel well. What applies the hadith about valuing health and time?

options.text: Stay awake all night to avoid any rest
Assume only paid work can make time valuable
Choose nothing thoughtfully because tomorrow is guaranteed
Plan a balanced mix of useful activity and suitable rest

questions.explanation: Valuing health and free time means using opportunities with care. A balanced, age-appropriate plan can include learning, kindness, worship, rest and play.

questions.question: Friends ask you to join an unkind joke. Which response applies the good modesty praised in the hadith?

options.text: Decline the wrongdoing without being unkind in return
Join because embarrassment makes every choice acceptable
Hide all future questions from your teacher
Insult the friends to prove you are better

questions.explanation: Good modesty can restrain us from wrong conduct. Refusing an unkind act does not require becoming unkind ourselves.

questions.question: A younger child correctly points out your mistake. What fits the hadith's warning about arrogance?

options.text: Reject the answer only because the child is younger
Accept the correction without looking down on the child
Change the subject to whose shoes cost more
Insist your age makes every answer right

questions.explanation: The warning includes rejecting truth and despising people. A correct point deserves consideration regardless of the other person's age.

questions.question: You hide a friend's pencil case as a prank. What should you do according to the report about belongings?

options.text: Keep it hidden until they offer a reward
Explain that joking removes the need for permission
Return it, apologize and stop taking things as jokes
Hide another item to make the prank funnier

questions.explanation: The report warns against taking belongings even in jest. Returning the item and putting the harm right respects the owner's rights.

questions.question: You are about to post a mocking comment that takes only seconds to write. What fits the hadith about careless words?

options.text: Post it because short comments cannot matter
Assume laughter makes the comment harmless
Add more insults so the message gets attention
Pause and consider its harm before deciding what to say

questions.explanation: A quick remark can still have serious consequences. Pausing helps us choose words more responsibly, including in online communication.

questions.question: You can choose your portion at a family meal. What applies thoughtful care for food?

options.text: Take a sensible amount and ask for more if needed
Take the largest amount to prove gratitude
Throw away safe food because the portion looks small
Eat unsafe food even when an adult warns you

questions.explanation: The report encourages care for food's blessing. Sensible portions can help avoid waste without forcing overeating or ignoring food safety.

questions.question: A Muslim friend has an important appointment and is not with you. What applies the hadith about dua in absence?

options.text: Wait until they can praise you for praying
Ask Allah to grant them what is good
Demand a present before making dua
Announce that your dua guarantees a particular result

questions.explanation: You can sincerely ask Allah for your friend's good while they are absent. The hadith encourages goodwill, not promises about a specific outcome.

questions.question: A friend privately shares an ordinary worry about a school presentation. What applies the hadith about entrusted speech?

options.text: Turn the worry into a group joke
Share it widely because it is interesting
Respect their privacy and ask before telling other classmates
Treat listening as permission to post it online

questions.explanation: Ordinary personal worries deserve care. If a confidence involves danger or harm, seek a trusted adult's help rather than keeping an unsafe secret.

questions.question: A neighbor gives your family a small, suitable homemade gift. What applies the hadith about modest gifts?

options.text: Say a gift counts only above a certain price
Ask why they did not buy something larger
Make fun of it in front of other neighbors
Thank them without comparing it with expensive presents

questions.explanation: The hadith discourages belittling a neighbor's gift. A gracious response recognizes kindness without turning the gift into a price contest.
